title: Territories Legislation Amendment Bill 2020
portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Communications

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that makes changes to laws affecting Australia's external territories, including Norfolk Island, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, and the Jervis Bay Territory.
The package would bring the legislative frameworks of these territories closer to those of the rest of Australia by amending numerous Commonwealth Acts.

The bill would extend the Bankruptcy Act 1966 to allow the Australian Financial Security Authority to deliver bankruptcy services to Norfolk Island, and a companion bill extends a related charges Act there as well.
changes: Amends the Norfolk Island Act to let the Australian Government arrange state-type service delivery on the island.
Extends the Corporations Act and related laws to external territories so all Australian companies face the same rules.
Lets the Australian Communications and Media Authority issue broadcasting licences in Norfolk Island.
Clarifies that the Privacy Act applies to bodies established under laws in external territories.
Updates the definition of 'Commonwealth public official' in the Criminal Code to include people acting under territory laws.
Treats Norfolk Island as a territory rather than a state for the Copyright Act.
summary.affected: The changes affect people and businesses in Australia's external territories, especially Norfolk Island, as well as Commonwealth agencies such as the Australian Financial Security Authority and the Australian Communications and Media Authority.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: The Bankruptcy (Estate Charges) Amendment (Norfolk Island) Bill extends the 1997 Act to Norfolk Island, ensuring consistent estate charges and equal treatment for bankruptcies there as in the rest of Australia.

speeches.speaker: Jason Clare
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Territories Legislation Amendment Bill 2020 and the Bankruptcy (Estate Charges) Amendment (Norfolk Island) Bill, arguing they ensure consistent Commonwealth support and law application for external territories. Labor moved a second reading amendment urging proper consultation with community stakeholders and the legal profession, including the Law Association of Norfolk Island and the Law Council of Australia.

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the Territories Legislation Amendment Bill and associated bankruptcy bill would align Norfolk Island and other territories with mainland Australia on governance, legal frameworks, and services. The speaker noted the bills extend national company and bankruptcy laws to Norfolk Island, improve privacy rights and review opportunities for residents, and ensure easier access to future government support packages.
